items.title: Bill Matthews Interview, 1959-03-10
items.q: I was playing with Morgan, Sam Morgan, all the parts.

ctx.x: We used a bass and a violin. You had that violin there. I don't care, that violin was a leader. He used to lead the band. So I got up, I got up and I said, Nene knew that I could play. Nene said, come on, Come on little baby. Come on little baby. Come on rest me up. Come on rest me up. We get up there and we play. I got up there and I played. Frank was living in the Algeist then. That's Frank at home too, Frank at home too. Frank was living in the Algeist then. Frank said, you look right, you learn how to play…
I was going to ask some more about those early days. Some of the, when you first played in a brass band, did you play snare drum or bass drum most of the time? Snare drum.

items.title: Bill Matthews Interview, 1959-03-10
items.q: fat p Sean I want you to take uh uh Albert Morgan and George Foster in charge at nine o'clock every morning

ctx.x: I wondered about that wrist action since drummers you know use their wrists so much and so loose

I think that's why you have that or did Vic make you do that that's right and see like uh fellas they don't have no other instrument they don't you know never learn how to play no other instrument it is you don't know the wrist way you see like you take lots of drummers right now they can't even make a clean roll no I mean like the old time drum they can't make a clean or the pop drum or though you know you know you can't make a clean roll but still they all know I know it you see our best drummer we got now in…
I saw Al Morgan this summer he told about being on the boat how he had to practice he told how he had to practice
